chain.label: Wind shear / upper-level temperature inversion near FL430
chain.trigger: a shallow temperature inversion layer, possibly an upper front, was reported at Bootheville, Appalachicola, and Tampa near the flight level of N125NE

chain.label: Learjet 25D's marginal high-Mach controllability / narrow buffet margin
chain.trigger: the aircraft's marginal controllability characteristics when flown at and beyond the boundary of its high altitude speed envelope

chain.label: Unauthorized overspeed warning horn cut-out switch installed
chain.trigger: N125NE was equipped with an overspeed warning horn cut-out switch, an unauthorized modification

chain.label: Copilot lacked Learjet rating/experience, fighter-trained for abrupt high-g inputs
chain.trigger: The copilot was not rated in the Learjet... he had accumulated 4,116 flight-hours, of which 65 hours were in the Learjet... a former military pilot

chain.label: Inconsistent AFM/training guidance on spoiler use in overspeed recovery
chain.trigger: the inconsistencies in aircraft flight manuals and flightcrew training programs regarding the use of spoilers to regain control

chain.label: Unexpected clear air turbulence encountered at FL430 near Covia Intersection
chain.trigger: an unexpected encounter with moderate to severe clear air turbulence

caused_by.evidence: the Safety Board concludes that moderate to severe clear air turbulence existed at FL 430 in the vicinity of the Covia Intersection when the accident aircraft entered the area

chain.label: Mach overspeed warning horn inhibited during the overspeed
chain.trigger: The lack of the Mach overspeed warning sound on the ATC tape probably indicates that the warning horn was disabled because of the cut-out switch

caused_by.evidence: the disconnection of the Mach overspeed warning horn with an unauthorized cut-out switch which resulted in the absence of an overspeed warning

chain.label: Flightcrew failed to reduce thrust promptly after turbulence-induced acceleration
chain.trigger: the primary reasons for the accident flightcrew's failure to recover were the lack of a timely thrust reduction

caused_by.evidence: the aircraft began to descend rapidly, and its speed began to increase shortly before the first staccato sounds were recorded
resulted in the absence of an overspeed warning that probably delayed the crew's response to the turbulence encounter

chain.label: Copilot's forceful high-g control wheel inputs, including inadvertent autopilot/yaw-damper disengagement
chain.trigger: it is probable that he could have accidentally disengaged the autopilot and yaw damper... his attempts to recover the aircraft by pulling on the control wheel probably resulted in a loss of roll control

caused_by.evidence: In a sudden upset, a pilot would reactively grab the control wheel in an attempt to maintain control of the aircraft
since he lacked experience in the Learjet, the copilot may have been more aggressive in his response to the upset... exerting more than 1.5 g's on the aircraft

chain.label: Pilot commanded spoiler deployment during overspeed, aggravating nosedown pitch
chain.trigger: put out the spoilers... extension of the spoilers would have further aggravated the situation by significantly increasing the pull force needed to restore the aircraft to level flight

caused_by.evidence: the pilot stated, "put out the spoilers"
the inconsistencies regarding the use of spoilers in training for an overspeed condition may have been responsible for the different response to the upset

chain.label: Progressive loss of control / uncoordinated roll (spin) from which recovery was not possible
chain.trigger: Can't get it up ... it's in a spin

caused_by.evidence: Since the aircraft was operating in a relatively narrow area of its flight envelope, the Safety Board considered the possibilities of a loss of control from transient conditions
the lack of a timely thrust reduction
an inadvertent disengagement of the autopilot and yaw damper
an inability to counteract the significant nosedown pitch forces caused by deployment of the spoilers

chain.label: Aircraft crashed into the Gulf of Mexico
chain.trigger: radio and radar contact with N125NE was lost about 104 miles west of Sarasota, Florida

caused_by.evidence: Northeast Jet Company, Learjet 25D, N125NE crashed into the Gulf of Mexico
Floating debris was located by a search aircraft and later recovered; the flightcrew was not found
